title: Why CXMT’s Memory Expansion Could Reshape the DRAM Market
gist: The post argues CXMT's predicted DRAM volume ramp (per Charles Kao, within two years) could pressure memory pricing around 2028, while TSMC's demonstrated BEOL memory embedded in logic interconnect layers could change processor memory architecture. The two are distinct markets — commodity supply vs. on-chip integration — and should be judged on yields, adoption and delivered costs rather than forecasts.

insights.claim: Charles Kao predicts CXMT will deliver large volumes of DRAM within two years, pointing to potential DRAM pricing pressure around 2028, though this remains an industry forecast rather than a guaranteed outcome.
insights.speaker: T
insights.so_what: 2028 DRAM pricing risk for incumbent memory makers; track CXMT capacity and yields.

insights.claim: If CXMT expands output, buyers gain cheaper memory and bargaining power, while established DRAM suppliers face pressure to defend margins, differentiate and reconsider capacity investments.
insights.speaker: T
insights.so_what: Bearish margin implication for incumbent DRAM producers; bullish for memory-heavy device and server makers.

insights.claim: Benefits from additional CXMT DRAM supply depend on product quality, customer qualification, and where those chips can actually be sold.
insights.speaker: T
insights.so_what: Export/geographic sales limits may cap CXMT's global price impact.
insights.quote: where those chips can actually be sold

insights.claim: TSMC has demonstrated back-end-of-line memory embedded in a logic chip's interconnect layers, which 2025 research described as denser than SRAM with low power and short access times.
insights.speaker: T
insights.so_what: Could shift on-chip memory capacity/area/energy trade-offs for AI and logic designs.

insights.claim: TSMC could make progress in BEOL memory integration without becoming a major standalone DRAM supplier, since integrated memory concerns processor architecture rather than component supply.
insights.speaker: T
insights.so_what: Don't read TSMC memory research as a threat to DRAM makers' commodity market.
insights.quote: TSMC could make progress in the latter without becoming a major supplier of standalone DRAM.

insights.claim: More conventional DRAM supply would not automatically resolve every constraint affecting advanced AI systems.
insights.speaker: T
insights.so_what: AI memory bottlenecks (bandwidth, proximity) may persist even if commodity DRAM gets cheaper.

insights.claim: Memory competition may intensify along two dimensions — manufacturing scale (CXMT challenging pricing) and technical integration (TSMC changing memory/energy/area trade-offs) — with decisive evidence being commercial yields, adoption and delivered costs.
insights.speaker: T
insights.so_what: Track yields and customer adoption, not forecasts or lab demos, before repricing memory names.
insights.quote: The decisive evidence will be commercial yields, reliable products, customer adoption, and delivered costs
